note: What's new on AGSIST, newest first. Only things that are live on the site.

items.title: Clearer ARC or PLC answers
items.line: ARC or PLC pages say why some expected payments are not shown, lead with the dryland answer, and show your farm total once you type base acres.

items.title: Clearer page titles and answers
items.line: Company bid pages name their locations, the USDA calendar sums up the last crop report from its own figures, and milk shows the 2025 all-milk average.

items.title: Only here lines skip a repeat
items.line: The Daily's Only here lines now come back only when something changed: new rain record counts, or a new rain report at your county's station.

items.title: No repeat lines for ZIP readers
items.line: With a ZIP, the Daily now gives the farm sales near you and your county's rain record once, and again only when new sales are recorded or the rank moves.

items.title: One name for each elevator
items.line: Elevators listed under an old or archived board name now show their own name and keep their basis history, on the home page, /cash-bids and the town pages.

items.title: Thirteen pages hold still while they load
items.line: Tariffs, sale barn prices, hay, break-even, store or sell, urea and seven more pages keep their room while the numbers load, so nothing jumps under your thumb.

items.title: Yield by state on phones
items.line: Quick stats shows each state's yield on phones and a pick-your-state menu; rain radar drops a bad NOAA square and links the spray forecast for your spot.

items.title: County rain names its gauge
items.line: County rain pages name the gauge behind the total, with the county-wide estimate beside it. A mountain snow site no longer leads a county page.

items.title: Old county rents marked n/a
items.line: State rent tables and Atlas titles show a rent over three survey years old as n/a with its last year, and list the counties NASS did not publish, with a county finder.

items.title: One state, every page
items.line: State pages for bids, rent, yield, rain, PRF and hail now link to each other, and ARC/PLC and PRF county pages name the nearest towns with bids.

items.title: Town bid pages, clearer
items.line: Town pages name corn and soybeans every time, keep elevators whose board went quiet with a labelled estimate, and mark boards that repeat another's bids.

items.title: USDA calendar: results first
items.line: The USDA calendar opens on what USDA printed against the trade, one card per number, then the next 5 reports. The full schedule and the details fold away.

items.title: Rain Print gaps
items.line: When a gauge reports several days of rain in one later total, Rain Print and the county prints count those days as reported together, not as gaps.

items.title: ARC or PLC method, in plain words
items.line: The ARC or PLC method now says plainly what the verdict compares and how past years came out; the fine print sits in the fold at the bottom.

items.title: Plainer ARC or PLC notes
items.line: Where a crop has little price history, ARC or PLC pages now say so in one plain line, and the crop pages fold their notices.

items.title: Tidier ARC or PLC county pages
items.line: ARC or PLC county and state pages gather the estimate notice and sources in one fold at the bottom.

items.title: Plainer Farmland Atlas county text
items.line: Farmland Atlas county reads say trend in plain words, and the sales note no longer points at a data file.

items.title: Tidier Farmland Atlas county pages
items.line: Farmland Atlas county pages keep their sources and terms in one short fold at the bottom.

items.title: A tidier grain bin calculator
items.line: The grain bin calculator page is tidier: the formula list is gone and sources sit in one closed note at the bottom.

items.title: A shorter USDA calendar page
items.line: The USDA calendar page is shorter: sources and terms now sit in one closed note at the bottom.

items.title: Cash bids: your state first, one-line email
items.line: Cash bids now shows your own state first before you type a ZIP, labels the table as estimates, and asks for your email in one line.

items.title: Shorter cash bid town pages
items.line: Cash bid town pages put where the bids come from in one short fold at the bottom.

items.title: Shorter cash bid state and company pages
items.line: Cash bid state and elevator company pages keep where the bids come from in one short fold at the bottom.

items.title: Shorter hail day pages
items.line: Each hail day page now keeps its sources, the radar caveat and the citation in one closed note at the bottom, so the storm figures read first.

items.title: Shorter hail map pages
items.line: The hail map and the state hail pages put sources and terms in one closed note at the bottom, so the map comes sooner.

items.title: Steadier drought, hail and milk pages
items.line: The Drought Monitor, Hail Map, Milk Prices and Desk pages no longer jump while they load.

items.title: PRF calculator fixes
items.line: The PRF calculator opens on hay ground, prints the cancellation date and the $30 fee, and no longer jumps while it loads.

items.title: Rain Print fixes
items.line: Rain Print keeps the nearest station with rain and snow records, offers the right spelling for a typo, and names the exact-spot option for a thin year.

items.title: Shorter county rain pages
items.line: County rain pages keep the station and its distance up top; sources and terms sit in one fold at the bottom.

items.title: Shorter cash rent pages
items.line: Cash rent pages put sources and terms in one fold at the bottom, so the county table comes sooner.

items.title: Steadier cash bid town pages
items.line: Cash bid town pages no longer jump while they load; the bid table stays where it is.

items.title: Shorter state yield pages
items.line: State yield pages put sources and terms in one closed note at the bottom, so the yield table comes sooner.

items.title: Cash bids holds still while it loads
items.line: The cash bids page no longer jumps while your saved ZIP's bids come in, so the email box and links below stay put.

items.title: The Daily says a thing once
items.line: A Daily line prints only when its number changed. New: a state basis line on weeks a state moves 5 cents, and fund positions on Saturday as the streak.

items.title: The Daily on one clock
items.line: The Daily labels each price as overnight or settle, quotes Jan beans once Nov is in delivery, and builds month to date from settles of one contract.

items.title: Farm sales page, made for phones
items.line: The farm sales page now opens with the map and the month's stand-out sales; the state and county lists sit in a fold below.

items.title: Rain page, made for phones
items.line: The rain page opens with a state picker and the records now; the full state list sits in a fold at the bottom.

items.title: Real maps on shared pictures
items.line: The Friday Chart poster and the cash bids share image now draw the real map of the states, with the small eastern states labelled in boxes beside it.

items.title: More auction results on county pages
items.line: Farmland Atlas county pages now list sold results from four more auction firms, in South Dakota, Missouri, Iowa, Kansas and Pennsylvania, with a link to each firm's page.

items.title: Farm sales read cleaner on a phone
items.line: Farm sale tables now stack one sale at a time on a phone with nothing cut off, and the fine print sits in one closed Sources and terms line at the bottom.

items.title: More room on your phone
items.line: On a phone, pages and cards now use more of the screen: narrower side margins and no double padding, so the numbers get the width.

items.title: A real US map
items.line: The state maps on farmland sales, cash rent, crop conditions and the farmland atlas now show the real shape of each state. Tap one for its number.

items.title: Sources tucked away
items.line: Long source notes and fine print now sit in one closed Sources and terms line at the bottom of each price and tool page, so the numbers come first.

items.title: GDDs by month is back on the home weather card
items.line: The home weather card has its GDDs by month chart back beside Rain by month. Tap any month on either chart for its numbers, or save the chart as a picture.

items.title: Saturday Daily: your local bid against last Friday
items.line: With your ZIP on file, the Saturday Daily now shows the top corn and soybean bid near you against that elevator's bid last Friday, with when it was posted.

items.title: The funds report countdown turns over on time
items.line: The bar at the top of the funds report now says the new report is out right at 3:30 PM ET, not up to a minute later, and its minutes tick over on the minute.

items.title: Funds chart labels stay apart
items.line: On the funds chart and its saved pictures, the 52-week high, low and latest labels no longer land on top of each other.

items.title: Fund positions: longs and shorts, not just the net
items.line: The COT page, the Funds this week email and the Daily now say how the funds' net changed: longs sold, new shorts, new buying or shorts bought back.

items.title: Harvest pace against USDA's five-year average again
items.line: Harvest by state shows the five-year average USDA prints in its weekly Crop Progress report again, filling the gaps the 2025 shutdown left.

items.title: Bin Print: map your bin yard
items.line: Map your bins on the grain bin calculator: each bin's bushels and what is in it now, a sheet to print, and a crew sheet whose QR code opens the yard on a phone.

items.title: County Print: one county on one page
items.line: Every Atlas county now prints on one page: what land rents for, what has sold, what farming there can earn and what could disrupt it, with sources and a QR code.

items.title: Pictures and printed sheets share one kit
items.line: Saved pictures and printed sheets for the funds report, Bin Print and County Print now come from one shared kit. They look the same as before.

items.title: Bids near your town: a picture and a printed sheet
items.line: Cash bid pages can save a picture or print a one-page sheet of the top 5 corn and soybean bids nearby, each with the time it was posted.

items.title: Save a picture of today's markets
items.line: The homepage can save a Today's markets picture: the futures board with when each price is from, your top local bid if set, and this week's big report.

items.title: Auction results on Farmland Atlas county pages
items.line: County pages now list farmland auction results the auction firm published, tract by tract, kept apart from recorded sales. First up: Wayne and Knox, Indiana.

items.title: Fund positions: a positioning map and options positions
items.line: Every trader group in every market, futures and options, placed in its own last 3 years on one map, plus options open interest and this week's 3-year extremes.

items.title: Every AGSIST forecast, graded in one place
items.line: The scorecard now lists every AGSIST forecast, each graded beside simple baselines that need no model, with rates held back until enough calls are graded.

items.title: Farm sale counts: one sale filed on several parcels counts once
items.line: A farm sold as several parcels, each filed with the full price, now counts as one sale on its total acres, so medians and counts are no longer inflated.

items.title: Sources stay folded
items.line: Every Sources list now stays closed until you tap it. The tar spot page also drops its leaf drawing and leads with the photos.

items.title: Tar spot photos
items.line: Eight field photos of tar spot on corn leaves and an ear husk, added to the identification section.

items.title: Tar spot of corn, in one place
items.line: How to tell it from rust, when to scout, when a fungicide pays, the 2026 product ratings, and a spray break-even calculator.

items.title: Source credits
items.line: Pages and emails that show USDA NASS numbers now carry the NASS notice, and our own averages, trends and estimates are marked as AGSIST calculations.

items.title: The Daily: price change since the week, month and year began
items.line: Corn, soybeans and wheat now show the change for the week so far and the month to date, plus a short weather note from USDA.

items.title: Home weather: weather and season totals only
items.line: Soil temperature, fall nitrogen and the spray read left the home page. Their own pages keep them.

items.title: Farmland Atlas map: what farms sold for, county by county
items.line: A map layer of median sale price per acre and sale counts for every county with a recorded sale in six states. Under 5 sales is marked a thin read.

items.title: The 52-week funds chart, up top
items.line: Pick a market to see a year of fund positions: long or short, this week's number, the high and low, and the price under it. Share it or save it as a picture.

items.title: Florida farm sales
items.line: Florida farmland sales from the state's sale files, 2008 on. Florida gives the month of each sale, so its sales show a month, not a day.

items.title: County rain pages add heat and frost
items.line: County rain pages get a weather fold: corn GDDs since May 1 against the station's own average, hottest and coldest days, and freezes, all measured.

items.title: Every detail of a farm sale, one tap away
items.line: Tap a sale's date on a county sale page, or Details on a card, for its deed type, acres, class, section, parcel and how its price compares. Names stay on their button.

items.title: A real farm sale on the home page
items.line: The home page shows a real recorded farm sale, its price an acre against the county's middle, and every county's sales in IL, IN, NJ, VT and WI.

items.title: Framed Rain Prints now come in oak or black
items.line: Pick an oak or a black frame for a framed Rain Print, same price; the picture on the page shows the one you pick, and What you get lists the frame, mat and glass.

items.title: Price fixes: soybeans on Jan, basis vs USDA's own normal
items.line: Soybean futures show January from first notice, so futures plus basis matches the cash bid; /basis compares USDA only with USDA's own normal.

items.title: Season so far in Local conditions
items.line: Rain and corn GDDs since Jan 1 and May 1 and for the last 30 days, each against normal, from your county rain page's station, all year.

items.title: Fund positions at a glance
items.line: The COT page and the home card now open with one plain line per market: long or short, how heavy, and the week's buying or selling. Get it every Friday by email.

items.title: Your ZIP works everywhere, and a slow connection still gets you bids
items.line: A ZIP typed on the cash bids page now carries to home, rent, ARC or PLC and custom rates. Slow live bids link the nearest town page with its time.

items.title: Home page soybeans on January too
items.line: The home page, the price ticker, /markets and breakeven quote the soybean month your elevator's basis uses (January from first notice).

items.title: Sponsor reports: private links, plainer numbers
items.line: Each sponsor's report now opens only from its own private link, shows no click rate until an ad has 100 views, and prices the sponsor's own states.

items.title: Feeder steer index: more barns
items.line: The feeder steer index now counts 80 to 94 barns a week through USDA's My Market News (55 to 92 before); the last three weeks came in $0.55 to $2.93 lower.

items.title: Put your county's rain on your site or in your newsletter
items.line: Each county rain page has a closed fold with a one-line rain box for websites, the same line in words to copy, and the monthly newsletter block.

items.title: Harvest pace back on Crop Conditions
items.line: Crop Conditions shows this week's harvest by state again, named by its own week, after USDA's last corn rating. Home store-or-sell starts from the first-half bid.

items.title: Custom rates: your state's own number first
items.line: Pick a state on Custom rates and its own survey number shows first, the middle across states under it; hauling shows each survey's miles.

items.title: Custom rates: quote my job and a rate sheet to print
items.line: Custom rates: a job quote at your state's survey averages, a rate sheet to print with your own price column, a diesel line, and an email when a new survey is out.

items.title: Farm diesel, propane and USDA fertilizer prices in My place
items.line: Fast Facts My place adds farm diesel and propane from USDA's dealer survey, and the fertilizer row shows the newer of co-op and USDA prices, dated.

items.title: Milk prices: this month first
items.line: The milk page opens with Class III, IV and all-milk, your area, what $1/cwt means on your herd, whether DMC paid, and the next months at futures.

items.title: Ethanol plants paying
items.line: The cash bids page shows what ethanol plants bid for corn in each state, with basis, from USDA's daily report, plus distillers grains and corn oil prices.

items.title: One label for the state basis everywhere
items.line: Every tool that shows a state's basis now says how many elevators it is the median of and how many companies run them, the same words as /basis.

items.title: USDA's state average beside our state basis
items.line: Each state basis number now says how many elevators it is the median of, and USDA's own state average for the day sits under it where USDA reports it.

items.title: USDA cash hogs, slaughter and export bids in the Daily
items.line: The Daily can now carry USDA's cash hog price and pork cutout, daily slaughter, ethanol plant and Gulf export corn bids, and new fuel and fertilizer prices.

items.title: Share today's bids from a town page
items.line: Cash bid town pages have a Share today's bids button: it sends the top nearest-delivery bid, the day it was posted and the town link by text or copy.

items.title: Feeder steer index: older weeks
items.line: The feeder steer index chart now reaches back to January 2024, figured from USDA's barn reports read through My Market News; 136 of 145 past weeks have a figure.

items.title: Our own feeder steer index
items.line: The cattle pages now show the AGSIST USDA feeder steer index: one weekly price for 700 to 899 lb steers from USDA sale barn reports, beside RMA's value.

items.title: New Jersey farm sales
items.line: Every recorded New Jersey farm sale by county, with acres from the state's assessment list and price per acre. In Field Scout, the Atlas and the land email too.

items.title: More in the Daily each morning
items.line: The Daily now carries the day's USDA reports and FSA signup dates, last week's harvest pace, fund positions after each Friday report, and your state's basis near the top.

items.title: Daily top stories link to the full story
items.line: On the web Daily and the home page, each top story title now opens the full story, with the publisher named underneath.

items.title: The home page opens on three jobs
items.line: The home page opens on Today near me, Sell grain and My field, with today's forecast for your ZIP; Rain Print, the rain gauge and new pages sit right under.

items.title: Rain and bids for your newsletter
items.line: A monthly block for co-op, Farm Credit and local paper newsletters: a county's rain last month and the state basis, ready to paste as text, HTML or an image.

items.title: ARC or PLC county pages open with the answer
items.line: Each ARC or PLC county page now opens with one plain sentence: what each main crop leans toward for 2026, its benchmark yield and the data date.

items.title: USDA report dates on your phone
items.line: Subscribe to USDA report dates from the futures pages and cash bids: one tap for your phone or Google Calendar, and each event links what the market priced in.

items.title: A new fact in the Daily every morning
items.line: The Daily's "I didn't know that" fact no longer comes back every two weeks, and it moves between topics: land, cattle, weather, markets, harvest and more.

items.title: The Daily has top stories, and no reruns
items.line: Each Daily now carries 3 to 5 top farm stories with links to the source, and never repeats a headline, number or story from the past week.

items.title: Read the sample letter full size
items.line: On the Rain Print page, tap the sample letter in the box to open it large enough to read.

items.title: Easier to tap on a phone
items.line: The grain bin depth slider and the hail map zoom buttons are bigger, so a thumb hits them the first time.

items.title: A Rain Print, made for you
items.line: Rather not make the print yourself? Call or text Sig, or leave your number. He makes two or three versions to pick from; you pay only if you order.

items.title: A new sponsor rate card
items.line: Advertise as the Daily Sponsor, a State Sponsor, the Cash Bids Sponsor or a featured elevator on its own town page; first month free, then a yes or no.

items.title: The homepage holds still while it loads
items.line: The top of the homepage no longer jumps down as it finishes loading, on a first visit or in the evening when the overnight futures line arrives.

items.title: Every recorded land sale
items.line: County land sale pages list every recorded sale of any size with its type, and the middle price counts bare farmland only, labeled.

items.title: County pages lead with land
items.line: Illinois, Indiana and Wisconsin county pages now open with land sale prices, newest sales, rent, nearest bid and rain, from your saved field if you have one.

items.title: Land values for North Dakota and Kansas counties
items.line: North Dakota and Kansas county pages show land values: the 2026 state survey of farmers and K-State's 2025 average of reported sales, each labeled.

items.title: Vermont farm sales
items.line: Every recorded Vermont farm and forest sale by county, with price per acre and current use. In Field Scout, the Atlas and the monthly land sale email too.

items.title: Farm sales easier to find
items.line: Every Farmland Atlas county page links its land sales, or says where the state's records stand. Rent pages, Fast Facts and search find county sales too.

items.title: Cleaner summer basis history
items.line: Summer rows where a few cents of basis were read as dollars are gone. Some summer weeks on Grain on the move shift up to 6 cents.

items.title: Big grain buyers near each town
items.line: Cash bid town pages and Atlas county pages now count the ethanol plants, oilseed crushers and export and rail elevators within 50 miles. Tap for names and miles.

items.title: What changed, on a real map
items.line: The Fast Facts county map now sits on a USGS map with towns and roads. Switch it between drought, bids, rent, sales and rain; tap a county for its line.

items.title: Farm loan cards, shorter
items.line: The farm loan cards on Atlas state pages now carry one short source line, linked to the reserve bank's ag survey page; how the numbers work is in one note per page.

items.title: Field Scout reads more of our own data
items.line: Field Scout now uses free USGS maps, loads county cards even when a lookup is down, and shows last year's crop, rain vs normal and the nearest bid up top.

items.title: Sales in your section first
items.line: Field Scout's sold land list puts sales in your field's own section, or one touching it, at the top and marks them, read from the legal descriptions.

items.title: A shorter menu, Ag stocks in it
items.line: The menu lists PRF, LRP and Rain Print once, adds Ag stocks under Prices and puts drought and manure under Field. The Illinois sale index is on the land sales page.

items.title: Forecasts from the National Weather Service
items.line: Home weather, spray, urea, grain drying, harvest or wait and planting date read the National Weather Service forecast. Soil temperature is measured at a station.

items.title: ZIP and town boxes use our own place list
items.line: Every ZIP and town box now finds your place in a list on our own site. Small Canadian towns are found by the weather station named for them.

items.title: GDUs from the PRISM daily grid
items.line: The GDU calculator and its embed add up heat from the PRISM daily grid (Oregon State), normals too. The Rain Print video no longer offers modeled wind.

items.title: Private ag raises on Ag stocks
items.line: Ag stocks now lists farm companies raising money online, with their SEC filings and how past raises turned out. These are high risk and hard to sell.

items.title: Every price says how old it is
items.line: Futures show their delay and a stale flag at the price, old cash bids show their posted date, and COT and crop conditions name survey and release days up top.

items.title: Farm loan repayment by Fed district
items.line: Atlas state pages now show what ag bankers in their Fed district reported for 2026 Q2: loan repayment and renewals against a year earlier, charted since 2010.

items.title: Short answers to what farmers ask
items.line: Seven pages now carry a short dated answer: farm bill, crop report, tariffs, USDA payments, cattle, beef supply, Argentine beef, screwworm, proposed BRAND heifer policy.

items.title: Cull cow prices from the sale barns
items.line: Boner, Breaker and Lean cow and slaughter bull prices at about 40 sale barns USDA reports, each with its own sale day, plus the middle Boner price.

items.title: Licensed dairy herds, US and your state
items.line: Licensed dairy herds from NASS by year for the US and your state, Wisconsin by month, with each year's net change. Also the 2014 to 2018 MPP margins, apart from DMC.

items.title: Farm bankruptcy filings on each state page
items.line: Each Farmland Atlas state page now gives its Chapter 12 filings for the 12 months to Sep 30, 2026, with 2025 and 2024 beside it, from the U.S. Courts tables.

items.title: Fewer pages, each one fuller
items.line: Ten pages joined the ones you already use, from crop size and what's priced in to the storm log, bids by state and past briefings. Old links still work.

items.title: Fast Facts opens at My place at once
items.line: With JavaScript off, a link to Fast Facts at My place opens right at that section instead of scrolling down to it.

items.title: The Daily tries again when a check holds it
items.line: A Daily draft that fails a number check is never posted. The next run writes it again and checks it again, so it goes out a little late rather than wrong.

items.title: Sale barn prices: four Kentucky barns back, and weights past page one
items.line: Owensboro, Somerset, Springfield and Stanford in Kentucky read again. About 20 barns now show the weight classes USDA prints after page one.

items.title: Sale barn prices: 37 more barns, most in Kentucky and Missouri
items.line: 125 USDA-reported barns, up from 88: 20 more in Kentucky, 13 in Missouri, 3 in Indiana, 1 in South Dakota. Beef-on-dairy steers no longer count in feeder averages.

items.title: Fall anhydrous: Wisconsin soil temperatures
items.line: Soil temperature at 4 in now comes from Wisconet's stations across Wisconsin too, each reading credited to its network. The fertilizer page adds Bartlett Co-op in Kansas.

items.title: Milk prices: the Upper Midwest order, and how close the futures came
items.line: Order 30's PPD for two years, what DMC would have paid since 2019 at FSA's margins, your order's PPD in the check reader, and the futures miss each month.

items.title: Milk prices: your area first, and read your own check
items.line: Your area's mailbox price leads the page, and a check reader values your milk at your own tests. The 2027 DMC signup is open to Dec 18.

items.title: Already on the Daily? Add your county
items.line: A link at the bottom of every Daily now turns on what changed in your county on Thursdays. It asks for your ZIP if we do not have it.

items.title: USDA calendar: the 2027 WASDE dates
items.line: All twelve 2027 WASDE dates, each at noon Eastern, from USDA's WASDE page. The 2027 NASS report dates are not posted yet and are not guessed.

items.title: Cushing Cooperative's phone number corrected
items.line: Now 715-648-5215, from the co-op's own bid page (it listed an Oklahoma number). Unconfirmed numbers for Prairie du Chien and Arcadia are no longer shown.

items.title: Your county this week, Thursdays in the Daily
items.line: Sign up for the Daily with your ZIP, tick the county box, and Thursday's email adds what changed in your county: drought, nearby corn bids, basis, land sales.

items.title: State basis: company counts match one more way
items.line: An elevator listed on another company's own bid page now counts with that company beside the state basis. Wisconsin shows one company fewer.

items.title: Fast Facts: what changed this week, on a map
items.line: Your place now opens with what changed this week (drought, top corn bid near you, county basis, new farm sales) and a state drought map.

items.title: Fast Facts: make the county's Rain Print your own
items.line: Under the county's year of rain, one link opens the same print in Rain Print, ready for your name.

items.title: Field Scout: back up your saved fields
items.line: Save every field, with its notes and photos, to one file and restore it on a cleared or new phone. GeoJSON and KML outlines restore too. Nothing is sent to us.

items.title: Cash bid pages load lighter
items.line: Town, state and company bid pages share one style file now, so each town page you open after the first is about a fifth smaller. They look the same.

items.title: Farm sales by county, and a monthly update
items.line: Recorded farm sales for every Illinois, Wisconsin and Indiana county, and a monthly update: biggest buyers and sales, unusual prices. Names show on a tap.

items.title: Pages agree on price delay, grading and privacy
items.line: One delay for futures prices (about 10 to 25 minutes), one grading rule on What's Priced In, and plainer privacy, ARC/PLC and cash bid net wording.

items.title: New farm sales near you, once a month
items.line: Pick a ZIP and 10, 25 or 50 miles: once a month, the farm sales recorded in it, with acres, price per acre and township. Illinois and Wisconsin; never who bought or sold.

items.title: Basis history kept when an elevator's listing was folded
items.line: An elevator whose two listings were folded into one keeps the older listing's basis record as its earlier history in My place.

items.title: Futures pages: the highest bid is a plain bushel bid
items.line: Organic, non-GMO, white and spring wheat bids no longer set the highest checked bid on the corn, soybean and wheat futures pages, and the bid is named under its own town.

items.title: Rain Print: a simpler set of layers
items.line: The crop layers (corn and soybean stages and the little plants) are off the Rain Print. An older link with them still opens, drawn without them.

items.title: County rain: the last week and month
items.line: Each county rain page now gives the rain its station caught over the last 7 and 30 days it reported, with the dates, next to the year so far.

items.title: Fast Facts for your place
items.line: Fast Facts has two tabs: your place by ZIP (bids, basis, rain, drought, rent, each dated and sourced) and the reference tables. Print makes a two-page sheet.

items.title: Feeder prices by region and weight
items.line: Weekly feeder steer and heifer prices at the USDA-reported barns we read, by region and 100 lb class, with the barns and head behind each price.

items.title: One place, all its numbers
items.line: Type a ZIP, town or county and get one page about it: where it ranks in its state, what sits far from its neighbors, and this week's bids, rain, drought and hail.

items.title: The Haymow: hay for sale and wanted
items.line: Post hay, straw or forage you have or need, free. Buyers and sellers find it by distance and call each other. No fees, no cut.

items.title: New menu and ZIP chip
items.line: The menu is now Prices, Livestock, Field, Money & Land and Daily. Save your ZIP once and the header chip takes you to bids near your town.

items.title: County stories
